page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance with a burstable CPU allocation profile, running on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8488C processor operating at 3.2 GHz, it provides 8 physical cores and 16 virtual CPUs through hyperthreading. The hardware includes a 105 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and hardware acceleration extensions such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8) alongside AVX-512. System memory comprises 64.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM at 5 GHz, delivering 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPUs, relying on EBS volume attachments and providing a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong single-threaded capabilities. The instance placed in the top 25% for single-core Geekbench score (2078.0), single-threaded gzip compression (33.17 GB/sec), text processing (2570.0), and prompt processing text generation for small LLM models (267.15 tokens/sec). Multi-threaded compute benchmarks generally align with middle 50% benchmarks across cloud providers, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 12210.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 27549.65. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 98.97 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput reached 27.93 GB/sec and Redis SET performance recorded 22.06 million operations per second.

The burstable CPU model offers favorable resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for workloads with intermittent compute spikes rather than sustained continuous utilization. Tradeoffs include potential performance throttles under prolonged max-load execution compared to non-burstable m7i counterparts. Equipped with 64 GB DDR5 memory and vector extensions, the m7i-flex.4xlarge is effective for general web application hosting, microservices, software compilation, text processing, intermediate database workloads, and lightweight machine learning inference.
